title: Factorized embodiment × task coordinates for invertible action policies
hypothesis: Separating embodiment geometry from task coordinates in shared invertible action space recovers held-out embodiment-task pairs with lower full bytes than independent policies while preserving one-step action success.

grid.adapter: two Givens rotation planes; angles sum embodiment and task factors

fresh.release_rule: Do not open fresh after exact native additive-angle alias or failed quality/storage gate.

controls: independent full policy matrix for each embodiment-task pair
pass_gate: Heldout nRMSE <=0.02, success >=0.95, >=25% fewer complete bytes than independent policies, one-step inference, and strict gain over native additive Givens composition.
fail_gate: FAIL Mirror-specific claim on native Givens alias, quality/success miss, savings below 25%, or no strict frontier gain.

compute.active_MACs: dense shared base plus four Givens rotations (two embodiment and two task, composed by summed angles); count independent dense matrix application separately
compute.wall_time: small CPU synthetic action batch only

boundaries: Synthetic linear action maps only; no multi-robot data, simulator, or hardware.
Embodiment and task IDs are known and charged; no identity inference claim.
Angle sums are deliberately the native additive control; Mirror must show benefit beyond this exact group composition.
